changes.before: In Témiscaming, Québec, around 80% of chimneys were damaged, indicating a Modified Mercalli intensity of VII. changes.before: The Newmark permanent displacement Dn quantifies the displacement induced by an earthquake accumulates in the sliding mass and is the performance measure from which the seismic coefficients are derived. The Dn(ky) curves relate, for each combination of geometry, material, and design scenario, the yield acceleration ky to the expected permanent displacement; they were computed with an ensemble set of AM88 (Ambraseys & Menu, 1988), JB07 (Jibson, 2007), SR08 (Saygili & Rathje, 2008), BT07 (Bray & Travasarou, 2007), and BM19 (Bray & Macedo, 2019), with reference magnitudes Mw = 5.5 and Mw = 6.5 assigned according to the seismic demand and 300 realizations per demand and are read at the fractiles q=1-pe. The horizontal pseudostatic coefficient kh is in turn derived from the allowable permanent displacement Da of the potentially sliding mass (Bray & Travasarou, Pseudostatic Coefficient for Use in Simplified Seismic Slope Stability Evaluation, 2009; Macedo, Bray, Abrahamson, & Travasarou, 2018); the coefficients are reported at four relative displacement limits, Da/Hs = 0.1, 0.4, 1.0, 2.5%, and the tables in Section 10.3 and Appendix E report, for the demands and scenarios analyzed, the coefficient at each limit, expressed as a percentage of the PGA.
changes.after: The Newmark permanent displacement Dn quantifies the displacement induced by an earthquake accumulates in the sliding mass and is the performance measure from which the seismic coefficients are derived. The Dn(ky) curves relate, for each combination of geometry, material, and design scenario, the yield acceleration ky to the expected permanent displacement; they were computed with an ensemble set of AM88 (Ambraseys & Menu, 1988), JB07 (Jibson, 2007), SR08 (Saygili & Rathje, 2008), BT07 (Bray & Travasarou, 2007), and BM19 (Bray & Macedo, 2019), with reference magnitudes Mw = 5.5 and Mw = 6.5 assigned according to the seismic demand and 300 realizations per demand and are read at the fractiles q=1-pe. The horizontal pseudostatic coefficient kh is in turn derived from the allowable permanent displacement Da of the potentially sliding mass (Bray & Travasarou, 2009; Macedo, Bray, Abrahamson, & Travasarou, 2018); the coefficients are reported at four relative displacement limits, Da/Hs = 0.1, 0.4, 1.0, 2.5%, and the tables in Section 10.3 and Appendix E report, for the demands and scenarios analyzed, the coefficient at each limit, expressed as a percentage of the PGA.

changes.before: The horizontal pseudostatic coefficient is derived in this assessment from the allowable permanent displacement Da of the potentially sliding mass (Bray & Travasarou, Pseudostatic Coefficient for Use in Simplified Seismic Slope Stability Evaluation, 2009; Macedo, Bray, Abrahamson, & Travasarou, 2018). The seismic demand and the fundamental periods established in the preceding sections allow the Dn(ky) relations between the Newmark permanent displacement and the yield coefficient to be computed; their inversion at the target exceedance probability yields kmax, and its normalization by the PGA transformed to the VS30 of each geometry–material combination yields kh, so that the result traceably links the deformation objective to the horizontal action employed in the stability verification. The yield acceleration ay represents the acceleration level at which the limit-equilibrium factor of safety equals unity and its dimensionless form is ky=ay/g; for each allowable displacement and target exceedance probability, the analysis determines the minimum ky threshold that satisfies the performance criterion, and that threshold is kmax, the coefficient applied in the pseudostatic limit-equilibrium verification. A factor of safety of at least unity under this applied coefficient indicates that the calculated yield coefficient meets or exceeds the required threshold.
